I believe this course required an unusually high amount of work, and in my opinion, Mr. Shaw’s grading and participation policies made it even more difficult. Compared to other philosophy classes, where participation is often graded more flexibly or even left partly optional, in this course we were required not only to speak regularly, but also to meet very specific expectations regarding what we said. Even when we asked questions or tried to contribute, our contributions were sometimes graded very low, which made participation feel stressful rather than encouraging.
Another issue was the ARR system used this year. We were not allowed to enter the sessions with our own notes, but instead had to rely on the printed material provided by the instructor. However, the topics were not explained to us sufficiently beforehand, and we were expected to study and fully understand them on our own. This created an unfair situation, especially compared to other courses where students have more flexibility in preparing and using their own notes. As a result, I believe many students, including myself, received unfairly low scores.
Overall, I feel that I received a very unfair grade in this course. It was a highly demanding and stressful semester, and I believe the grading system and participation expectations should be reconsidered. I would like to emphasize that Mr. Shaw may personally be a kind person and a capable teacher, but I still think that the way this course was conducted and graded was unfair to students.

instructor:
I would like to share my disappointment regarding this course. Throughout the semester, this was the class I devoted the most time and effort to. Compared to students in other sections, our workload felt noticeably heavier, with assignments almost every week. Because of this, it was difficult to fully use the attendance allowance, as most classes involved required tasks. Spending so much time on a pool course was emotionally and mentally exhausting. The assignments were often presented as particularly challenging, which I understand may have been intended to contribute to learning. However, over time, this approach became discouraging. When course averages are compared across sections, it was disappointing to see that the additional effort and difficulty did not translate into more balanced outcomes. I believe the grading was fair in the sense that it reflected the work submitted. Still, the overall difficulty level made it hard to feel rewarded for the amount of effort invested. Many tasks felt more demanding than what I expected from a course at this level. Although I respect and generally like the professor, this course left me feeling more worn out than motivated.
What saddened me most was realizing how much of my study time was absorbed by this single course, often limiting my ability to focus on others. I hope that in the future, the exams and assignments can be designed in a way that better aligns with general academic expectations, allowing students to feel that their effort is both meaningful and fairly reflected.

Because the grading standards were not always transparent, it was challenging to predict how assignments and exams were assessed.
